summary: The study investigates the plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) of cobalt thin films using cyclopentadienylcobalt dicarbonyl [CpCo(CO)2] combined with hydrogen, nitrogen, ammonia, and argon based plasma gases. The research focuses on the influence of process parameters such as plasma power, process pressure, and substrate temperature on film composition and properties. The study also examines the role of plasma gas composition in determining the material properties of the resulting films, with a particular emphasis on minimizing impurities and achieving high-quality, low-resistivity films.
evidence: Plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) of cobalt (Co) using cyclopentadienylcobalt dicarbonyl [CpCo(CO) 2] combined with hydrogen, nitrogen, ammonia, and argon based plasma gases was investigated. The authors studied the influence of process parameters (e.g., pulse times, plasma power, and substrate temperature) on film compositions and film properties. The occurrence and prevention of sputtering effects due to ion bombardment at high plasma powers were discussed. Beyond those results, precise information about the impact of different plasma gas compositions on the resulting film properties was obtained.
